prompt: The supplied HTTP service has a measured latency regression between commits `base` and `candidate`: under the provided 400 requests/s workload with the same 20k-record dataset and runtime configuration, p95 rose from about 85 ms to 230 ms while correctness remains green. Reproduce both builds with the fixture's warm-up and five repeated runs, record p50/p95/p99, throughput, CPU, allocation/GC, I/O wait, and saturation, then profile the candidate before editing. Establish which resource/path explains the regression, make the narrow correction, and repeat the identical comparison. Do not lower workload, change response semantics, or report a single lucky run as the fix.

requirements: base and candidate builds are available from the same fixture
400 rps, dataset, runtime configuration, and resource limits are fixed across comparisons
warm-up plus five measured repetitions are defined
functional correctness tests pass on both starting builds
profiling and system resource counters are available

falsifiableChecks.assertion: Baseline and candidate are measured under the same workload, dataset, configuration, warm-up, and resource envelope with repeated p50/p95/p99 observations.
The proposed cause is supported by profile/resource evidence that explains the measured delta rather than by speculation or a code diff alone.
The post-fix candidate is retested under the identical protocol, restores the stated performance budget without reducing workload, and keeps correctness green.

evidence: profile/resource evidence and identical post-fix rerun
the bottleneck hypothesis explains the measured resource delta

requiredEvidence: post-fix identical benchmark plus correctness output
